newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sega aims for 1-1.5 mln Saturn Japan sales in '97.
newsitem.headline: Sega aims for 1-1.5 mln Saturn Japan sales in '97.

text.p: Sega Enterprises Ltd said on Thursday that it aims to sell between one million and 1.5 million units of its Sega Saturn 32-bit game machine in Japan in the current calendar year.
"We want to ship out 1-1.5 million units this year," Toshiro Kezuka, a Sega director, told reporters, referring to Sega Saturn sales in Japan.
He was speaking at a news conference to launch new game software for the Sega Saturn machine. The software, named Virus, will go on sale in August.
The software is being jointly developed by Sega, Japanese software house Hudson Soft Co Ltd and record company Avex.
A Hudson official told the same news conference that the partners were aiming for a situation in which one in five owners of Sega Saturn game machines would buy the new software.
He did not specify a time frame for the targeted sales.
Sega has said that it has sold around 4.5 million Sega Saturn machines.
